questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** It depends on the boot. For my Blundstones, I wouldn't treat finished, pretreated leather out of the box, but I would treat distressed styles like Rustic Brown. After that, I treat them when they look or feel dry, not on a fixed schedule.

**Out of the box**
- Blundstone's own FAQ, which I read in my videos, says most of their boots come pretreated, so they "do not recommend treating them out of the box" [1].
- The exception is rustic and distressed leathers. According to that FAQ, these "do not carry the same pretreatments as a finished and oiled leather" [2].
- For my Rustic Brown pair, I recommend conditioning them: "I don't recommend you keep it dry" [3].
- In 2019 I first thought my distressed pair might be untreated. In the water test they held up fine, and I took that claim back [4]. I still said I'd treat them anyway [5].

**How often**
- My latest view is from 2022: I "personally probably do too little", and I treat mine when I feel they need it [6]. Other people are more regimented. It depends on how much you wear them and where you go, so use your intuition [6].
- Signs they need it: they look or feel dry, or water isn't beading on top. In that case they need more wax or more oil. Also clean them regularly, because dirt wears the leather down faster [7].
- In my 2019 review I was more specific: you may have to wax them "every month maybe every week" if you're hard on them [8]. Treat that as a rough guide for heavy use. My later advice is to go by how the leather looks and feels.
- When I do treat them, I always go in this order: clean, condition, wax [9].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, they get tighter the first time they get wet, mostly in the waist. After that, wearing them loosens them up again. I haven't tested repeated washes beyond that.

**Latest advice (2023 and 2025)**
- When I compared shrunk 501 STFs with rinsed 501s, I found that if you put them in the dryer, they would be a lot smaller from the start. [1]
- My advice is not to toss STFs in the dryer or rinse them in very hot water. You can then get a really nice fit. [2]
- I also bet that with frequent wear they would stretch out to about the same size. [3]
- Because of the shrinkage, I usually say to go two sizes up. [4]

**What happened to my own pair (2019 and 2020)**
- In 2019 I soaked mine, and they definitely slimmed up, mainly in the waist. [5] Length barely changed. [6]
- A week later the waist and thighs had stretched enough that I could wear a belt. [7]
- I ignored Levi's sizing and bought a 29 waist and 30 length. In 2020 I said I could barely pull them on at first, but a year later they were a really good fit. [8] I also said I would have gotten a 32 length. [9]

**Sizing rule**
In 2021 I said Levi's advice is correct: size up two in the waist and two inches in length. [10] So for you, buy two waist sizes above your usual size and an extra two inches of length.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
Applying my rule, I'd buy a **35 waist and 32 length** in the 501 STF. I haven't covered the 502, so I can't say how its sizing compares with the 501.

**The rule I follow now:** Levi's recommends going two sizes up in the waist and two inches longer than you'd normally wear, and in 2021 I said that after four pairs of 501s I'd found Levi's is correct [1]. In 2025 I repeated that you should usually go two sizes up [2]. In my Wrangler comparison I went from a size 30 to a size 32 [3]. For you, 33x30 becomes 35x32.

**How my view changed:** In 2019 I ignored Levi's advice on my first pair [4]. I bought a 29x30, could barely pull it on, and said I was glad I'd gone small on the waist. By 2020 I said I definitely should have gotten a 32 length [5]. My later advice is the Levi's rule, not my first-pair approach.

**One caveat:** I noted that a 36 might not exist when sizing up from a 34 [1]. I haven't said what to do if a 35 isn't available in your case, so check what sizes are on offer.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
I cuff mainly because I can't settle on one hem length, and cuffing lets me adjust it. I also cuff when jeans come out too long or too wide for my style.

**Indecision about length (2021):** I can never decide between no break, half break or full break, so every pair feels like the wrong length. Besides settling on one specific fit, which I plan to do when I buy my perfect-fitting pair, cuffing is the only solution I've found for now. [1]

**Wider legs and my style (2020):** On my Levi's 501 STF, I cuffed them because I don't think my current style suits wider-legged pants left uncuffed. I also said I should have bought a 32 length. [2]

**Too-long jeans (2019):** When I first tried the 501s, I said it's all about length for me. If jeans look too long, they just look bad, and that's the first and foremost thing. I added that the cuff can't be thick. [3]

**A trade-off:** Cuffs make your legs look shorter. I like the long-leg look, so that is a downside. [4] I also think wider pants look better with a higher hem, because excess fabric crumples at the shoe and breaks the clean silhouette. [5]

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly yes, though by 2023 I'd hedged.** In 2022 I said the 3335s beat the 1907s. In September 2023 I said they still might be my favorite Red Wings, but I wasn't sure, and I was selling them.

**Where I landed in 2023:** I'm on record saying the 3335s are my favorite Red Wings of all time. I added that "they still might be but they probably not" the 875s, the 1907s or the Iron Rangers, because those all have characteristics I really like [1]. I still like the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight and nimble feel [1]. But "they're going" [1].

**October 2022, when I reviewed the 3335s:** I called them my favorite boots I've ever had and said "They beat my Blundstones, they beat the 1907s, they beat the 875s" [2]. My reasoning was that I'm hiking and walking in the woods, not doing heritage work, so for me they're a dramatically better all-around boot [2]. If you need a tough boot, the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so those are the ones to go for [2]. In January 2023 I still called the 3335s my favorite Red Wings to date [3].

**Earlier on the 1907s:** In 2021 I said the 1907s are Red Wing's best heritage boots by far, and that if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing, I think you should get them [4]. I also said I highly recommend them [5].

**Bottom line:** For hiking and walking around, I preferred the 3335s in 2022. For a tougher work-style boot, I'd point you to the 1907s. By late 2023 I was no longer sure the 3335s were my favorite, and I was selling them.

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, I'm still a big fan of Blundstones, but I'm retiring my 585s to make room in a smaller collection. They aren't going because I've soured on them.

**My latest view (Sept 2023):** My 585s were the subject of my first ever video. I've worn them constantly, and they've held up. The leather is beat up and shiny, and they're "probably my most water resistant boots through it all." I said "bluntstones are just incredible I'm a big fan of them I've always loved them," and that I've noted some people really don't like them. I still said "it's time to retire those bunnies." [1][2]

**The heavy-duty Extremes:** I'm also letting go of my Blundstone super heavy-duty work boots. I thought they were waterproof, but they're just very water-resistant nubuck. I still called them "insane boots" because of the steel toe, fire and electrical hazard resistance and the added height. They have to go because my collection is shrinking. [3]

**How my view developed:**
- In 2019, soon after buying them, I said I recommended them "100%" if you're going to treat them. Otherwise I'd get plastic or Gore-Tex boots. I also said they were by far my favorites of the three or four boots I had then. [4][5]
- My main gripe then was that the soles can't technically be replaced. [6]
- In 2020, after a year, I said they were performing about how I'd hope for the price. [7]

Overall my feelings on Blundstones haven't changed much. I liked them in 2019, they held up, and I still rate them in 2023. I'm just retiring this pair.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
I'd go with Solovair over the Made in England Dr. Martens, unless you specifically want the Dr. Martens look or heritage. I've said this consistently across my videos. In September 2023 I was still positive on my Solovair monkey boots. I'd sell them "probably only to get another pair of monkey boots" [1], and I said "through all of that I really like these boots" [2].

**Price and value**
- When I compared them in May 2023, the Solovairs were about $40 cheaper. I said "you're getting a better boot that costs less" [3].
- On the Made in England boots alone, I said they're "probably not" worth the extra $90 over the cheaper Thailand pair [4]. They're for big fans of the brand [5].

**Construction and comfort**
- Solovair has "thicker heavier more robust felted midsoles" [6].
- Solovairs have a shank, so they're "a bit more comfortable over long periods of time" [7].
- Solovair sells its soles on its website, and I said this is why the boots have "a way way higher lifespan" than Dr. Martens [8].

**Leather**
- In 2022 I said the Made in England leather "will age fine" and is "probably on par with solar bears" [9].
- In 2023 I added that Solovair "does use full grain leather" on certain models [10]. You need to check the specific model, because that varies.

**Where Solovair falls short**
- My Solovair monkey boots had a quality-control problem. My only real gripe is the laces: "that's my only gripe with solar" [11].
- Sizing was off for me. One pair came in "like clown shoes", so I suggest sizing down a half size and checking the comments [12].

**When I'd still pick Made in England**
- If the yellow stitching matters to you, Solovair doesn't do it [13].
- If you're a big Dr. Martens fan who wants boots made the way the old ones were, "you have to go made in England no question" [14].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
**I haven't covered multi-day hikes in Blundstones, so I can't say they're right for a 4-day trip.** From what I did say, I'd be cautious about relying on them for that.

**Ankle support:** I took mine up and down a few mountains in Maine and they held up, but I said they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. They got a little scuffed, but they "held up well" [1].

**Break-in:** If yours aren't fully broken in, be careful. When I started running and walking the track in mine, I got "big fat gross blisters like break-in blisters for boots" until they were broken in after two to three weeks [2].

**Water:** After a year untreated, I stood in a pond and my feet stayed mostly dry. My conclusion was that if you're crossing a brook or stream, or standing in some mud for a bit, "you should be good" [3]. They're water resistant, not waterproof. Keep the leather treated if you want that to hold up [4].

**What I'd pick for long hikes:** I haven't tested any boot on a multi-day hike. Of the others in my collection, I said the Jim Green Razorbacks have "a lot of padding so if you're going hiking for a long time that's good stuff" [5].

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
For you, I'd go with the Muji tee as the best mix of cost and quality, and Uniqlo if you want the cheapest option. I can't give you a specific size, because I haven't covered sizing for your height and weight.

**Muji or Uniqlo**
- In September 2025 I said the Uniqlo shirt at about $20 is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price." [1]
- I also said that if you're taller or wider, you'd want Muji. It costs a few dollars more, but it's "significantly longer and a good deal wider." [2]
- In June 2025 I said the Muji shirt feels justified at its higher price: "It does feel justified to be $10 more though." [3]
- I'd say that's the safer pick for your build.

**Other value options**
- The Front General Store tee is a $40 shirt made 100% in Japan, with great proportions and feel. [4]
- The House of Blanks tee at $35 is made in Canada and showed zero torque. I called it "truly an outstanding value." [5]
- If you want character, I'd go Front General Store. I said "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store. Tomorrow I might be feeling House of Blanks." [6]

**Size**
- The only thing I can tell you is what I look for: shirts with a lot of space across the shoulders, and tees that "flatten me out." [7]
- Since you want room, the longer, wider Muji is where I'd start. [2]
- I'd be careful with Los Angeles Apparel. It fit me "a bit like a tent," but I said that sizing down one might make it a winner. [8][9]

hybrid.answer:
I haven't covered whether Ralph Lauren quality has dropped over time, so I can't confirm your impression.

**What I have said about RL quality**
- Judging it is hard because the brand does everything. In my view it's "so hard to talk about Ralph Lauren quality specifically because what is Ralph Lauren besides everything?" - In my fall thrift video, I called a vintage Ralph Lauren blanket-lined denim jacket "one of the best cold weather Colder Weather denim jackets ever" and said I was "really liking Ralph Lauren lately." [2]
- On chinos, I said Ralph Lauren is "probably doing a similar ply or similar weight fabric" to J.Crew, which I guessed and didn't test. I also said you can find them on eBay for 20 or 30 dollars. [3]

I haven't compared old and new Ralph Lauren pieces side by side the way I did with Levi's. If you tell me which item you mean, I can say whether I've covered it.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
**You're not alone, and I'll narrow it down for you, though I can't name one shirt for everyone.** In my latest t-shirt roundup (September 2025) I said the best tee depends on your preferences: "It just has to line up with your preferences to be the best t-shirt." [1] With that caveat, these are the three I'd point you to.

- **Cheapest good option: Uniqlo.** At $20 it's "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price." [2] If you're taller or wider, I'd get Muji instead: it costs about $4 or $5 more but is significantly longer and wider. [3]
- **Best all-around: J. Press x American Trench.** I was stuck between it and 3Sixteen, but I'd "might go with J Press just because I like the rougher hand feel." [4]
- **Best value with character: The Front General Store.** For value picks I chose it or House of Blanks, depending on taste. If you like lots of character, go Front General Store; if you want perfectly smooth with no torque, go House of Blanks. [5]

**If you want to spend more:** in my "Supremes" category I said Lady White could be my favorite, but I picked Merz b. Schwanen that day, as "I feel like MSB eekes out just a little bit." [6] In the Japanese category I'd pick Wonder Looper for its more universal fit, and in the heavyweights I'd pick American Giant, which is a little lighter and fits more universally. [7]

**One more:** I forgot Bronson in that video, and it usually wins or comes close in t-shirt comparisons. [8]

questions.question: Do you have any particular favorites for more athletic builds? I sometimes have trouble with high quality tees being tight on the shoulders and boxy around the waist

hybrid.answer:
I haven't singled out tees for athletic builds, so I can't name a favorite for shoulders and waist specifically. Here is what I've said about fit that might help.

**Shoulders:** I like a lot of space across the shoulders, and the J. Press x American Trench shirt is one I called a "good freaking fit" on that point [1]. It was my pick in the all-arounders category in 2025 [2].

**Not boxy:** I mentioned the Asket tee as what I imagine "very jacked or slim men wearing at coffee shops because it just flows, feels like glass" [3]. That's the closest I've come to talking about muscular guys. I haven't said how it fits through the shoulders or waist.

For other fit details:
- **Merz b. Schwanen 2M15:** I like its unique fit, especially across the neck and chest. I called it very distinctive and gave it my Supremes pick for 2025 [4]. The 215 and the 2M15 both have an underarm gusset, which gives a tighter sleeve more range of motion [5][6].
- **Wonder Looper:** I said its fit is "much more universal" than Samurai's, which is cropped and wide [7].
- **Muji:** If you're bigger, it's "significantly longer and a good deal wider" than Uniqlo [8].

**Seams:** Back in 2023 I said I prefer shirts with side seams, because you can usually finagle the fit a bit more, and tubular shirts feel like "a tube" [9]. If you get a boxy waist, a side-seamed shirt is where I'd start.

My general advice is to look for a brand that matches your body type better [10].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**I'd pick the 1907 if you're choosing between the two moc toes.** The main difference is the storm welt, and for about $10 more you also get a removable leather footbed and leather laces. I've also said the 875 and the 1907 each have characteristics I like, so the 875 is not a bad choice.

**Welt construction**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. I call Goodyear welts "incredible", "really durable" and "pretty water resistant" [1].
- The 1907 has the storm welt (Red Wing sometimes calls it Norwegian-like). To me the storm welt is invaluable [2].
- From what I've seen on Reddit, Red Wing's version is probably just another leather strip stitched onto the welt. I'm not sure that's exactly right [3].

**Price and what you get**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more, but I don't think that's a real price gap [4].
- It comes with Red Wing's inner leather footbed, which you can typically buy separately for $40 [5].
- It also comes with leather laces, typically $15 [6].
- Counting the storm welt too, I still say it's a better deal [7].

**What they share**
- Both have crepe soles, which I think break down faster than the Vibram sole on the 3335 [8].
- Both are more beefily built than the 3335s, so they suit you better if you need a tough boot [9].

**My overall view**
- In 2021 I said the 1907s are Red Wing's best heritage boots by far, and that I'd get them if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing [10]. I repeated that recommendation a couple of months later [11].
- By 2023 I put the 3335s first among Red Wings, but I said the 875s, the 1907s and the Iron Rangers all have their own characteristics that I really like [12].
- I do have a caveat: leather welted boots aren't great in water. I wear my 1907s day to day, but functionally they don't do a ton for me in the rain [13].

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Uniqlo is my pick for the best budget shirt. In my latest roundup (Sept 2025) I said its $20 tee is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. If you can spend about $40, Front General Store is the upgrade. I haven't compared Uniqlo directly against Pro Club.

**Uniqlo:** I call it your starter t-shirt, and I describe it as "Open-ended kind of rough." [2] In mid-2025 I said that for $15 it's very good, with a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle a lot [3]. In 2024 I said it may be the best bargain tee [4].

**Front General Store:** It's a $40 shirt made 100% in Japan [5]. In my Sept 2025 ranking I picked it over House of Blanks for that value category, though I said "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store," so that pick could change [6]. In 2024 I called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" [7].

**Pro Club:** I only covered it in 2024. It was the roughest shirt on that list, but I said "all in all I like everything about it" [8]. I gave it a softness score of 4 out of 10 [9].

**Hanes:** In 2024 I called it "your classic $10 great shirt" [10]. It was much softer than Pro Club, at 7 out of 10 [11]. By 2025 I was more cautious about the very cheapest mass-market brands. I named Hanes among the giants that rush through production [12], and all five shirts I had from those brands had a defect [13]. So I'd take Uniqlo over Hanes for a bit more money.

**Bottom line:** Uniqlo is the best budget shirt for most people. Front General Store is my choice if you want more character and Japanese construction. Pro Club and Hanes are cheaper but rougher or less consistent.

questions.question: Would you recommend this [Barbour Bedale] or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
**I'd go with the Bedale for what you describe.** It's the one I'd pick as a rain jacket, a windbreaker and a light spring layer in one. The Flint and Tinder is a good jacket too, but I haven't tested it in rain the way I have the Barbour.

**Why the Bedale (my 2025 view):**
- It's the lightest fabric of all the waxed jackets I compared, and I said "any time of year, you could toss on your Barber and be super comfortable." [1]
- It has a throat latch, hood snaps and storm cuffs, which help in bad weather. [2]
- In my 2021 review I liked the storm flap behind the zipper, which stops water running through it. [3]
- A brand-new coat of wax didn't leak at all in my shower test. [4]
- Get the hood. I highly suggest it, since without one the jacket is only fine on days like a dry fall one. [5]

**Caveats on the Barbour:**
- A waxed jacket isn't a dedicated rain jacket. I said "it's not a designated rain jacket," though I said that about waxed jackets generally. [6]
- Water resistance depends on the state of the wax. As the patina develops you lose a little practicality, so you'd need to re-wax it. [7]

**Flint and Tinder:**
- In 2025, in a segment sponsored by Huckberry, I said it's built for everyone, is lighter weight and goes with anything. [8]
- It's lined, so you don't get wax on your skin. That's a plus for a light spring jacket. [9]
- The price is $300, and I still find it hard not to recommend. [10]
- In my 2023 comparison I was less sweeping. I said it was for a specific man who is not me, though I'd love it slightly modified. [11]
- I haven't covered its rain or wind performance in these videos, so I can't say it beats the Barbour there.

**Bottom line:** for the rain-and-wind side, I'd pick the Bedale with the hood. If you mostly want a comfortable, lined, light jacket, the Flint and Tinder is a good choice.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
The con was about the unlined jacket I tested in that video, not the lined versions. That's a fair point, and my view has softened since then.

**What I meant in 2023:** The jacket in that video was Huckberry's basic unlined model at $228. I said the one con it shares with the Rogue Territory jacket is that [they are not lined](6n9t0SDne44). I explained that I "personally always like aligning on wax jackets just so the wax isn't touching your clothes or your arms or something like that" [1]. It was a personal preference, and I still called the jacket "fantastic" and said you'd be happy with it [2].

**The lined versions:** I know they exist and like them. In 2022 I noted that Huckberry offers [an unlined option](cpgTqqJLNZY), which means the standard one is lined. In 2023 I said there is a wool-lined version, but it comes in "dramatically more limited quantity" [3]. In 2025 I said the standard trucker is lined, so you don't get wax on your skin, and that I haven't yet tried the wool-lined one [4].

**Where I am now (2025):** I said I usually still want a liner on wax jackets because the wax gets on your skin [5]. But I added that "in my old age... I kind of see why you wouldn't line something" [6]. So I'd now call an unlined jacket a trade-off rather than a flat con.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
I haven't directly compared the fit of the 3335s and the 875s in my videos, so I can only tell you how the 3335s fit.

**3335 fit:** I went true to size and they fit fine [1]. They have a slim profile and taper down. With thin cotton socks I had no discomfort or tightness. With wool socks my toes felt squished and I couldn't wiggle them much [1].

**Versus the 875s:** The only comparison I made is about construction. I called the 1907s and 875s "definitely more beefily constructed" than the 3335s [2]. That is about build, not fit, so I can't tell you whether the 875 runs roomier or tighter in the toe.

If you're deciding between them, the one thing I'd take from this is to be careful with the 3335's snug toe area if you wear thick wool socks.
